title: The City’s street-permit average excluded ten projects still waiting

beats.text: Thirteen completed street improvement permits averaged 584.6 days.

visual.sub: The deadline was for an agency performance goal

beats.text: Developers held the plans for 282.9 days between submissions.

visual.heading: Where the completed cycles spent time

beats.text: The utility commission’s reviews overlapped other City reviews.
The published average left out ten permits still open.

visual.kicker: Ten still-open cycles already averaged 646.6 days

visual.label: Ten still-open cycles already averaged 646.6 days

beats.text: Treasure Island’s entry had reached 1,404 days.

visual.label: Ten still-open cycles already averaged 646.6 days

beats.text: The City accounted for 645 of those days.
For simple permits, 69% met a separate 40-business-day goal.

visual.label: A separate bureau table uses business days and a different denominator

beats.text: That clock paused while other agencies or applicants reviewed the plans.

visual.kicker: A separate bureau table uses business days and a different denominator

beats.text: Public Works later cut its first response from 102 days to 20.

visual.kicker: The reported improvement was in first response and review rounds

beats.text: A first response can lead to another round.
Treasure Island reported eight rounds on its Stage 2 plans.

visual.label: A project with a long-running permit reached construction

beats.text: By October 2026, crews were installing utilities and a sewer pump station.
